subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy in core, and what policy shape should be approved first?
rationale: The request changes the browser egress security boundary and public config/approval semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the policy UX, timeout, metadata-blocking, and compatibility contract.

options.title: Stage explicit allow/block policy first
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase with documented allow/block semantics, metadata endpoint behavior, and upgrade-safe config before adding interactive prompts.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to a user-approval UX with timeout, rate limiting, audit logging, and channel/web UI delivery semantics across browser navigation paths.

options.title: Keep current strict/opt-in model
options.body: Leave private-network access as strict by default with explicit trusted-environment opt-in and hostname exceptions.

recommendation.title: Stage explicit allow/block policy first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase with documented allow/block semantics, metadata endpoint behavior, and upgrade-safe config before adding interactive prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history across browser SSRF helper work, policy docs, and security/config tradeoff decisions visible in this path.
